Formulation
Laura Parkinson presents with contact dermatitis likely caused by occupational exposure to cleaning products without protective gloves. Her type 2 diabetes may contribute to the general dryness of the skin. Limited social information and lifestyle factors such as minimal alcohol use, non-smoking status, and the stressor of new job responsibilities are noted.

Mental Health Care Plan Details

Principal Problem:
- Patient Goal(s): Relieve symptoms of dermatitis to perform job duties effectively
- Clinical Goal(s): Reduce inflammation and dryness, prevent further exacerbation
- Actions (Patient): Wear gloves while working, apply prescribed creams/emollients
- Actions (Clinician/GP): Prescribe steroid creams and emollients, arrange follow-up if no improvement

Secondary Problem (if applicable):
- Patient Goal(s): Manage general skin dryness
- Clinical Goal(s): Hydrate and maintain skin moisture
- Actions (Patient): Regular application of emollients
- Actions (Clinician/GP): Continue monitoring diabetes management

Patient Education, Emergency Care & Relapse Prevention
- Education Given: Yes. Topics Covered: Importance of wearing gloves, proper use of emollients/steroids, signs of worsening condition
- Early Warning Signs of Relapse/Worsening: Increased dryness, spreading dermatitis
- Coping Strategies: Use of gloves, consistent use of prescribed treatments
